To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The most important mammographic predictors of the size and presence of invasive carcinomas are the size of the malignant microcalcification cluster, the number of malignant microcalcification clusters, and the presence of a mass.

the presence of a microcalcification lesion without a mass on a screening mammogram is a marker of a higher likelihood of an invasive cancer and that the size of the invasive component in the cancer associated with the microcalcification lesion is greater in lesions that are larger on screening mammography.

the presence of a mass and the number of microcalcifications in mammographic microcalcification lesions (MCLs) without a mass are independent mammographic predictors of the size of invasive carcinoma associated with MCLs without a mass.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an algorithm that is capable of detecting and segmenting microcalcification clusters in digital mammograms.
the development of a new method for detecting the presence and size (volume) of invasive carcinomas in mammograms associated with malignant micro-calcification lesions.
the development of new methods for breast cancer screening.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the mammographic findings of a mass, architectural distortion, and/or clustered microcalcifications in a breast cancer patient are associated with the presence and size, and possibly the grade, of the invasive component.
mammography has a high sensitivity and specificity in screening for breast cancer.
mammographic features are not reliable for predicting the size of an invasive carcinoma in a microcalcification cluster.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found that the mammographic features of the malignant microcalcification lesion were associated with the presence and size (diameter) of the associated invasive carcinoma.
we found a significant correlation of the presence of invasive carcinoma with mammographic features of the associated calcifications.

the presence of microcalcifications on screening mammography is a marker of increased breast density and increased risk of breast cancer.
